Humanoids

ZUTIK researches software for humanoids integrated with factory systems

TECNALIA leads six research organizations developing navigation, manipulation and OT/IT integration, targeting TRL 4 laboratory demonstrators.

TECNALIA ↗7 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 1

Adapting existing platforms

TECNALIA described ZUTIK as a research effort to prepare Basque industry for reliable humanoid integration. The project will develop algorithms and software components for existing robot platforms rather than build a new humanoid. It addresses complex factory environments, object handling and coordinated whole-body motion.

A modular integration architecture

Research covers perception, bipedal locomotion, safe navigation, multi-fingered and whole-body manipulation, and skill-based programming. A modular, vendor-agnostic architecture is intended to connect these capabilities with factory OT/IT systems. The aim is to coordinate humanoids within existing production infrastructure and support future integration across platforms.

Laboratory validation comes first

The consortium includes TECNALIA, AUTOTECH ENGINEERING, IKERLAN, MONDRAGON MU-EPS, EHU and INVEMA, with eight industrial companies contributing through a business committee. TRL 4 laboratory demonstrators will use scenarios such as kitting, assembly, inspection in complex spaces and internal logistics. Further readiness work will be required before production deployment.
